exchange.text:
NVDA's gross margin fell sharply in Q1 fiscal 2026 (quarter ending April 2025), dropping to 60.5% — the lowest reading across the eight quarters shown. The decline was abrupt relative to the gradual erosion that preceded it, and the margin recovered in subsequent quarters, suggesting a one-quarter disruption rather than a structural shift.

**Trend across the window.** NVDA's gross margin had been drifting lower from 78.4% in Q1 fiscal 2025 (ending April 2024) to 75.1% in Q2 fiscal 2025 (ending July 2024), 74.6% in Q3 fiscal 2025 (ending October 2024), and 73.0% in Q4 fiscal 2025 (ending January 2025). The pace of decline accelerated dramatically in Q1 fiscal 2026, when NVDA reported 60.5%. The margin then rebounded to 72.4% in Q2 fiscal 2026 (ending July 2025), 73.4% in Q3 fiscal 2026 (ending October 2025), and 74.4% in Q4 fiscal 2026 (ending January 2026).

**What stands out.** The Q1 fiscal 2026 print is the weakest quarter by a wide margin in the series shown. Every other quarter sits between 72.4% and 78.4%, so the 60.5% reading is an isolated trough. The recovery that followed brought the margin back close to the level seen in Q3–Q4 fiscal 2025, though it remained below the Q1 fiscal 2025 peak.

**Counterpoint.** The sharp rebound in Q2 fiscal 2026 and the continued improvement through Q4 fiscal 2026 argue against reading the Q1 fiscal 2026 margin as a new baseline; the trajectory after the dip is upward, not flat or deteriorating.

**What the data cannot tell.** The figures show the magnitude of the decline but not its cause. No management commentary or segment-level cost detail is included in the evidence provided, so the driver of the margin compression in that quarter is not identified here.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** A one-time inventory or product-mix charge compressed margins in that single quarter, given the immediate recovery to 72.4% in the following quarter.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** A shift in product mix toward lower-margin configurations during a transition period weighed on the quarter, given that revenue still grew 12.0% quarter-over-quarter in the same period.
